observation: Residents and eligible property owners were consulted on parking changes. Published support by street section was 86%, 100%, 88% and 56%, showing materially different views across the four sections. See source for the separate segment results.
representativeness: Restricted to eligible residents and property owners along specified street frontages; not representative of the whole electorate.

observation: Development Victoria reports strong community support for redevelopment of the former VicRoads site and recognition of a need for more homes; feedback also sought better public spaces, walking/cycling links, green space and heritage recognition.
representativeness: Specific project consultation; participant count and response distribution not stated on summary page. Not an electorate-wide measure.

observation: The Kew MP raised reported resident concerns about dust, construction noise, amenity and changes to the local environment, including the design and performance of noise walls.
representativeness: A parliamentary statement reporting constituent concerns; no count or independent survey supplied.

observation: The Kew MP reported that residents were concerned about the planned removal of a city-bound bus stop near the Eastern Freeway entry ramp and raised the need for more frequent Route 200 services to Bulleen Park and Ride.
sentiment_target: bus stop removal and service frequency
representativeness: A parliamentary question reporting constituent concerns; no count or independent survey supplied.

geographic_scope: Barkers Road; Willsmere Road / Earl Street
observation: The Kew MP raised road-safety concerns and called for pedestrian crossings at Barkers Road and the Willsmere Road/Earl Street roundabout, citing near misses, injuries and petitions said to have attracted thousands of signatures.
representativeness: A parliamentary statement; petition totals and underlying responses should be independently verified before quantitative use.

geographic_scope: Boroondara LGA - contextual proxy, not Kew electorate only
source_name: City of Boroondara - Community Plan consultation results
observation: Across the municipality, the survey's highest-ranked focus areas included green space, sport and recreation, personal safety/crime/policing, active travel, respect and inclusion, and rates/cost of council services. Workshop priorities differed, highlighting active travel, green space, housing affordability/diversity and preventing inappropriate development.
representativeness: More than 5,000 community survey participants and 156 workshop participants; municipality-wide, not electorate-specific.

geographic_scope: Edgevale Road between Cotham Road and Stirling Street
observation: For proposed weekday 2-hour parking restrictions, 40% of eligible respondents supported the changes and 60% opposed them. Council said the response threshold was met but the support threshold was not, so existing restrictions remained.
representativeness: Only nearby residents with a frontage on Edgevale Road and eligible absent owners were invited. Response count and denominator are not published on the summary page.

geographic_scope: Adeney Avenue east side north of Argyle Road
observation: 64% of eligible respondents supported weekend daytime permit-zone restrictions. Council said the 55% support threshold was met and the restrictions would be introduced. The response count is not stated on the summary page.
sentiment_target: specific Adeney Avenue weekend parking changes
representativeness: Restricted to residents, property owners and people eligible for a residential parking permit along the specified frontage; not representative of the electorate.

observation: In the first-stage consultation on a public toilet at Eglinton Reserve, 79 of 93 participants (85%) supported the proposal; 11 (12%) opposed it and 3 were unsure. More than 80% of participants lived in Kew.
sentiment_target: public toilet proposal at Eglinton Reserve
representativeness: 93 self-selected consultation participants; over 80% lived in Kew. Local and relevant but not a representative sample of Kew electors.

observation: For the revised toilet location, 32 of 64 recorded responses (50%) supported it, 8 (12.5%) supported a toilet in the park but suggested an alternative location, and 24 (37.5%) were not supportive. The 64 responses comprised 61 survey participants and 3 written submissions; over 95% of survey participants lived in Kew.
sentiment_target: specific revised toilet location at Eglinton Reserve
representativeness: 64 recorded responses, not a representative sample. 61 survey participants; over 95% lived in Kew, plus 3 written submissions from Kew residents.

issue: Kew Junction public space and amenity
observation: Council's Kew Junction Place Plan consultation invited ideas about valued public spaces and possible improvements. The page records 80 map contributions, but does not publish a sentiment distribution in the material reviewed. This is an engagement-volume signal only.
representativeness: 80 map contributions; contribution count does not reveal support, opposition or representativeness. Do not use as a sentiment score.

geographic_scope: Kew, Kew East and Balwyn North
observation: Council consulted residents about their bus-use and transport needs in the northern suburbs to support advocacy to the Victorian Government. Consultation closed on 26 February 2026. The public page reviewed confirms the consultation but does not publish a response breakdown.
representativeness: Geography includes Kew, Kew East and Balwyn North; no participant count or result distribution published on the page reviewed. Not Kew-only.
